configurePresets.name: native64
configurePresets.displayName: Native Linux x86_64 -- SDL2 + both GL devices, NO Pixomatic
configurePresets.description: 64-bit native build (ufront 2.54). Same engine and the recovered Karma as `native`, at LP64 instead of -m32. NO PIXOMATIC, and that is not a policy choice: the prebuilts are i386-only on BOTH platforms (pixomatic_linux.a is a 32-bit i386 archive; the Windows side is an import lib against a PE32 i386 DLL) and there is no source to rebuild from, so -SOFTWARERENDERER does not exist here. 32-bit remains the DEFAULT (`native`): it is what the suite is calibrated on, and it is the pointer-width CONTROL arm of decomp/test/ut2004/ktrace_gate.sh, which compares a 64-bit candidate against it byte-for-byte.

configurePresets.name: native
configurePresets.displayName: Native Linux x86 -- SDL2, both GL devices + Pixomatic, one binary
configurePresets.description: 32-bit native build. SDL2Drv + OpenGLDrv (desktop GL) + GL4ESDrv (GL->GLES2 translation) + PixoDrv (Michael Abrash's software rasterizer, -SOFTWARERENDERER) all in ONE binary; pick at startup with -OPENGLRENDERER / -GL4ESRENDERER / -SOFTWARERENDERER. Karma is ON (the RECOVERED sources -- USE_KARMA_DECOMP defaults ON), so this has vehicles and ragdolls; `native-nokarma` is the physics-off control. Builds in build-native/ -> ut2004-pixo.bin. [ufront 2.34]

configurePresets.name: native-sse
configurePresets.displayName: Native Linux x86 -- the ktrace CONTROL arm (32-bit, SSE float math, no Pixomatic)
configurePresets.description: ufront 2.58. The 32-bit pointer-width control for decomp/test/ut2004/ktrace_gate.sh: the same recovered Karma at -m32 with -msse2 -mfpmath=sse, so the ONLY variable against the 64-bit candidate is the pointer width. `native` cannot be that control: it is -march=pentium -msse with x87 doubles at 80-bit and produces trace md5 81b06b0cf715, never the reference c31ed77b7323. No Pixomatic (it is not needed for a trace and it is the open -O2 defect), so the binary is build-native-sse/Source/SDLLaunch/ut2004.bin, NOT ut2004-pixo.bin.

configurePresets.name: physics
configurePresets.description: gl4es stack with WITH_PHYSICS=ON. Builds in build-physics/.

configurePresets.name: wasm
configurePresets.description: Emscripten gl4es web build: -O2 + DWARF + assertions + exception catching. The everyday dev build — named stacks and readable errors while the engine still runs at a playable speed. NOT the small one: DWARF plus un-cleaned-up inlining makes it the largest of the three. Builds in build-wasm/. Run `source ~/emsdk/emsdk_env.sh` first (sets EMSDK).

configurePresets.name: wasm-debug
configurePresets.description: Emscripten gl4es web build: -O0, nothing inlined, every local live. Reach for it when the OPTIMISER is the suspect — a bug that shows at one -O level and not another is almost always undefined behaviour. ~5x the wasm and a much slower boot. Builds in build-wasm-debug/.

configurePresets.name: wasm-perf
configurePresets.description: Emscripten gl4es web build: -O3, assertions off, no debug info -> smaller/faster. Builds in build-wasm-perf/. Run `source ~/emsdk/emsdk_env.sh` first.

configurePresets.name: windows64
configurePresets.displayName: 64-bit Windows (MinGW-w64 cross) -- WITH the recovered Karma
configurePresets.description: The x86_64 Windows build, and the reason it exists is Karma: MinGW cannot link MathEngine's MSVC-mangled prebuilts, so a Windows build could never have physics until the recovery replaced them with portable C. It does now. LLP64 (`long` is 4 bytes where Linux's is 8) while pointers are 8 on both, so this is the only target that exercises that combination. Validated by the SAME ktrace as every other target -- `decomp/test/ut2004/ktrace_run.sh` runs a .exe under wine -- and its trajectory matches the 32-bit control. Builds in build-windows64/ -> ut2004.exe. ufront 2.58: USE_PIXOMATIC=OFF is stated here because the preset inherits ON from `windows` and the 64-bit Pixomatic guard is a configure-time FATAL_ERROR, so `cmake --preset windows64` could not configure at all; the 2026-09-07 build had been configured with the flag passed by hand.

configurePresets.name: windows
configurePresets.displayName: Windows x86 (MinGW-w64) -- SDL2, both GL devices
configurePresets.description: 32-bit Windows build (MinGW-w64 cross from Linux). SDL2 + BOTH GL render devices (OpenGLDrv desktop GL and GL4ESDrv) plus PixoDrv, picked at startup with -OPENGLRENDERER / -GL4ESRENDERER / -SOFTWARERENDERER. ufront 2.54: PIXOMATIC IS NOW ON. Its pixomatic.lib is a pure IMPORT library (all members are `pixomatic.dll`), so the DLL is a LOAD-TIME dependency -- measured: objdump lists pixomatic.dll among the exe imports and the Delay Import Directory is empty, i.e. a missing DLL means the process does not start at all, not a renderer that is merely unavailable. The DLL is now VENDORED at Thirdparty/Pixomatic/Bin/pixomatic.dll (PE32 i386) and staged beside the exe by SDLLaunch/CMakeLists.txt, so the artifact is self-contained rather than only runnable inside a retail install. Karma is ON here too (the recovered sources; the old note that MinGW cannot link MathEngine is pre-recovery history). Builds in build-windows/ -> ut2004-pixo.exe. [ufront 2.33, SDL2 2.34, Pixomatic 2.54]
